items.title: Decide whether to file an objection (Einspruch)
items.action: Decide whether to object to the fine notice; if you disagree, send a written objection (or declare it in person for the record) to the Ordnungsbehörde by the deadline shown.
items.consequence: If no objection is filed in time, the fine notice becomes final (rechtskräftig) and you must pay the full amount.

data.title: Traffic Fine for Mobile Phone Use While Driving (Bußgeldbescheid)
data.summary: The Ordnungsbehörde of Stadt Musterhomburg (Saar) issued a fine notice (Bußgeldbescheid, Az. OWi-26-118430) for using a mobile phone while driving on 16 October 2026, imposing a total of €132.00 (€100 fine, €28.50 fee, €3.50 delivery costs) and 1 point in the Fahreignungsregister. The notice was formally delivered on 24 November 2026, opening a two-week window to file an objection (Einspruch).
data.explanation: This is an official fine for holding and using a mobile phone while turning your vehicle. You may accept it and do nothing (it becomes final automatically), or you may object (Einspruch) if you disagree — the app shows the deadline for that. Only after the notice becomes final (if you don't object by the deadline shown) should you transfer the total amount; paying earlier is not requested. Non-payment after it becomes final could lead to enforcement action, though this letter does not spell that out. If you're unsure whether to object, consider getting legal advice (e.g. from a traffic lawyer) before the deadline passes.
